requirements.quote:
Figure 2 omits the EndOfEarlyData message, which is not used in QUIC;
   see Section 8.3.
requirements.condition: When implementing the TLS handshake message flow for QUIC.
requirements.required_behavior: Omit the EndOfEarlyData message from the QUIC TLS handshake.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using or sending an EndOfEarlyData message in QUIC.
requirements.why_checkable: A handshake trace or message dispatcher can be checked for the presence of EndOfEarlyData.

requirements.quote:
Likewise, neither ChangeCipherSpec nor KeyUpdate
   messages are used by QUIC.
requirements.condition: When implementing TLS message handling for QUIC.
requirements.required_behavior: Exclude ChangeCipherSpec messages from the QUIC TLS message flow.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using or sending a TLS ChangeCipherSpec message in QUIC.
requirements.why_checkable: A QUIC TLS handshake trace and message-generation paths can be inspected for ChangeCipherSpec messages.

requirements.quote:
Likewise, neither ChangeCipherSpec nor KeyUpdate
   messages are used by QUIC.
requirements.condition: When implementing TLS message handling for QUIC.
requirements.required_behavior: Exclude TLS KeyUpdate messages from the QUIC TLS message flow.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using or sending a TLS KeyUpdate message in QUIC.
requirements.why_checkable: A QUIC TLS handshake trace and message-generation paths can be inspected for TLS KeyUpdate messages.

requirements.quote:
Data is protected using a number of encryption levels:

   *  Initial keys

   *  Early data (0-RTT) keys

   *  Handshake keys

   *  Application data (1-RTT) keys
requirements.required_behavior: Use the Initial, Early Data (0-RTT), Handshake, or Application Data (1-RTT) encryption level, as applicable.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using an encryption level outside the four enumerated levels.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's encryption-level enumeration and packet-processing paths can be compared with the four listed levels.

requirements.quote:
Application data can only appear in the early data and application
   data levels.
requirements.condition: When carrying application data in QUIC.
requirements.required_behavior: Place application data only at the Early Data or Application Data encryption level.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Placing application data at the Initial or Handshake encryption level.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet traces or frame-level tests can correlate application data with the encryption level used.

requirements.quote: Handshake and alert messages may appear in any level.
requirements.condition: When carrying a TLS handshake message in QUIC.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat every defined encryption level as structurally permitted for handshake messages.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Rejecting a handshake message solely because of its encryption level, absent a more specific rule.
requirements.why_checkable: Level-validation logic can be tested with handshake messages at each defined encryption level while controlling for more specific message rules.

requirements.quote: Handshake and alert messages may appear in any level.
requirements.condition: When carrying a TLS alert message in QUIC.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat every defined encryption level as structurally permitted for alert messages.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Rejecting an alert message solely because of its encryption level, absent a more specific rule.
requirements.why_checkable: Level-validation logic can be tested with alert messages at each defined encryption level while controlling for more specific message rules.

requirements.quote:
In the 1-RTT handshake, the client is
   unable to send protected application data until it has received all
   of the handshake messages sent by the server.
requirements.condition: During a 1-RTT handshake, before the client has received all handshake messages sent by the server.
requirements.required_behavior: Wait until all server handshake messages have been received before sending protected application data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending protected application data before all server handshake messages have been received.
requirements.why_checkable: A handshake trace can compare the client's first protected application-data send with receipt of the server's complete handshake flight.

requirements.quote:
This application data can be replayed by an
      attacker, so 0-RTT is not suitable for carrying instructions that
      might initiate any action that could cause unwanted effects if
      replayed.
requirements.condition: When selecting instructions to carry in 0-RTT application data.
requirements.required_behavior: Use 0-RTT only for instructions whose replay cannot cause unwanted effects.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Carrying instructions in 0-RTT when replay could initiate an action with unwanted effects.
requirements.why_checkable: Replay is concrete, but whether an application action has an unwanted effect depends on unspecified application semantics, so this text does not define an objective protocol-level check.
